answer: A voyage through an agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may attest to others' work. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge: it earns only small fees until its attestations match the consensus of established peers, and any false attestation slashes its stake. An attacker spawning many fake identities must fund each one's stake, so a sybil swarm's cost grows linearly with its size, while honest agents echo each other's verified work and build reputation that compounds. Forging a thousand credible voices costs a thousand stakes, not one script.
